question: Mahesh has ₹1617 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Vijay and Ajay and asked them to invest it at 10% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Vijay and Ajay got same amount after 15 and 16 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Mahesh give to Vijay?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate of Interest = 10% = 1/10.

Multiplying factor for compound amount = (1 + 1/10) = 11/10.

Difference in time period between the investments = 16 − 15 = 1 year.

Ratio of Vijay's share to Ajay's share = (11/10)¹ = 11 : 10.

Vijay's share = 11 / (11 + 10) × 1617 = 11/21 × 1617 = 11 × 77 = 847.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹847.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount Mahesh has = ₹1617

Rate of Interest (R) = 10% compounded annually

Time for Vijay (t₁) = 15 years

Time for Ajay (t₂) = 16 years

**Formula Used:**

Compound Interest Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 
 Total: ₹1617

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Mahesh give ₹V to Vijay and ₹A to Ajay.

⇒ Amount received by Vijay after 15 years = V(1 + 10/100)¹⁵ = V(1.1)¹⁵

⇒ Amount received by Ajay after 16 years = A(1 + 10/100)¹⁶ = A(1.1)¹⁶

⇒ According to the question, their received amounts are equal: V(1.1)¹⁵ = A(1.1)¹⁶

⇒ V = A(1.1)¹⁶ − ¹⁵

⇒ V = A(1.1)¹

⇒ V / A = 11 / 10

⇒ The ratio of shares of Vijay and Ajay = 11 : 10

⇒ Total ratio parts = 11 + 10 = 21 parts

⇒ 21 parts = ₹1617

⇒ 1 part = 1617 ÷ 21 = ₹77

⇒ Vijay's initial share (V) = 11 parts = 11 × 77 = ₹847

**∴ The correct answer is ₹847.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Division of Sum for Equal Compound Amounts

When a total sum is divided into two parts P₁ and P₂ invested at R% for t₁ and t₂ years respectively to yield equal amounts, the ratio of their principals is given by P₁/P₂ = (1 + R/100)t² − t¹.

Compound Interest Growth Factor

The final amount A under compound interest is given by A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ. The term (1 + R/100) is the multiplying factor that grows the principal every successive year.

Difference Between Simple and Compound Interest

For the first year at a given rate of interest, both simple interest and compound interest yield the same amount. In compound interest, the interest for successive years is calculated on the previously accumulated amount, whereas in simple interest, it is calculated only on the initial principal.
